title: Add caching + request coalescing for telemetry query service used by Incident Bot v2
creator: Miles Thornton
body:
Problem
- Incident Bot v2 pulls saturation/health signals via the Telemetry Query Service (TQS). During incidents, responders frequently trigger multiple bot interactions in a short time window (thread replies, "refresh", "expand", modal pagination).
- We have seen bursts cause TQS latency spikes/timeouts and, in worst cases, amplify load on upstream metrics backends. This makes bot cards unreliable exactly when we need them most.

Goal
- Keep bot response time predictable under incident load by adding caching + request coalescing in TQS.
- Bound query cost and prevent thundering herds when multiple Slack actions request the same data.

Scope
- Implement a cache layer inside TQS for the bot-facing query endpoints.
- Add in-flight request coalescing (single flight) per cache key.
- Add guardrails: max key cardinality, TTLs tuned for incident response, per-request budgets/timeouts, and explicit degraded behavior.

Non-goals
- Re-architect metrics storage.
- Add new telemetry signals (handled in ENG-5423 and related work).

Design
1) Cache keys
- Cache key must capture ALL parameters that change the result:
  - caller (incident-bot) + endpoint version
  - environment (prod/staging)
  - region
  - service/route identifiers
  - tenant scope (tenant_id OR "all-tenants"; must be explicit)
  - query window (start/end or lookback)
  - metric set (gpu_util, queue_depth, kv_cache_pressure, admission_backpressure, etc)
  - aggregation + downsample
- Key format (string):
  - tqs:v2:{env}:{region}:{service}:{route}:{tenant_scope}:{lookback_s}:{agg}:{metric_set_hash}

2) TTL policy (defaults)
- Fast-moving saturation summary: TTL 15s
- Error budget burn / SLO widgets (if served via TQS): TTL 30s
- "Expand details" / modal pages: TTL 30s (same base key + page params)
- Add stale-while-revalidate: serve stale up to 2x TTL if upstream is timing out (include "stale" flag in response metadata; bot renders banner).

3) Request coalescing
- Maintain an in-memory map of in-flight promises keyed by cache key.
- If a request for an identical key arrives while one is in-flight, await the same promise (with its own caller timeout).
- Ensure cancellation/timeout semantics do NOT cancel the shared upstream call; only the waiting client.

4) Storage
- Phase 1: in-process LRU (bounded by count + bytes) to ship quickly.
- Phase 2 (optional): Redis/shared cache if we need cross-instance hit rates. This ticket ships Phase 1 but keeps interfaces compatible.

5) Guardrails
- Hard cap on key cardinality drivers:
  - Require normalized route identifiers (no raw URL path fragments).
  - Limit tenant-scoped queries to explicit tenant_id OR "none"; do not accept arbitrary label filters from the bot.
- Budgeting:
  - Per request timeout: 1200ms (bot card wants <2s end-to-end).
  - Upstream query timeout: 800ms with 1 retry (jittered backoff) only for idempotent read queries.
- Circuit breaker:
  - If upstream error rate > X% over 1m, switch to "cache-only" mode for bot callers for 60s.

6) Response shape expectations for bot
- Always return something quickly:
  - If live query succeeds: fresh data.
  - If live query fails but cache has prior value within stale window: return stale + reason.
  - If no cached value: return empty + deep links (dashboards/traces) and a short "manual next step" snippet.

Acceptance criteria
- p95 TQS latency for incident-bot caller <= 600ms under a synthetic burst (50 concurrent requests for identical keys, 10 distinct keys).
- Cache hit rate >= 70% during incident-bot interaction bursts in #incidents (measured via TQS metrics).
- Coalescing works: for identical keys, upstream query count ~= 1 per TTL window (validated in load test).
- Clear observability added:
  - tqs_cache_hit_total{caller,endpoint}
  - tqs_cache_miss_total{caller,endpoint}
  - tqs_cache_stale_served_total{caller,endpoint}
  - tqs_singleflight_join_total{caller,endpoint}
  - tqs_upstream_queries_total{backend,caller}
  - tqs_request_duration_ms{caller,endpoint}
- No increase in upstream metrics backend QPS during Slack "refresh storm" compared to pre-change.

Implementation notes
- Use a size-bounded LRU; key/value size tracking should be approximate but enforced.
- Cache values should store:
  - payload
  - fetched_at
  - ttl_s
  - backend_used
  - is_stale flag computed at read
- Log sampling: only log cache misses + upstream timeouts at 1% to avoid flooding during incidents.

Rollout plan
- Gate behind a server-side flag in TQS: tqs.bot_cache_v1
- Enable in staging for bot integration tests.
- Prod rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours.
- Rollback: disable flag (no schema changes).

Risks / open questions
- In-process cache may reduce effectiveness if we scale TQS horizontally; mitigated by coalescing per instance and short TTLs. If hit rates aren’t sufficient, we’ll follow up with Redis.
- Ensure cache key normalization doesn’t accidentally collapse distinct queries (validate with unit tests on key builder).

References
- Related tickets: ENG-5423 (saturation signals), ENG-5425 (Slack ack/retry), ENG-5429 (load shedding)
- Incident-bot repo: PR-1854 (Slack modal pagination + caching behavior in bot UI layer), PR-1865 (timeout handling improvements)
- Infra/guardrails: redwood PR-29152 (rate limits/circuit breakers for diagnostics endpoints)
- Internal ticket: INT-3341 (telemetry query timeouts from incident-bot)
activity_log: 2025-02-13 Miles Thornton created ticket; scoped as P0 after INT-3341 + on-call reports of bot card timeouts.
2025-02-18 Logan Wright aligned on caching primitives + required metrics for hit rate/coalescing visibility.
2025-02-21 Jacob Stein implemented singleflight coalescing + LRU cache interface; added basic hit/miss metrics.
2025-02-26 Nadia Rahman reviewed key normalization (route/service/tenant) to avoid high-cardinality cache keys.
2025-03-04 Devon Price confirmed bot behavior with stale responses + banner copy for degraded mode.
2025-03-10 Aisha Bello requested explicit circuit breaker behavior for bot callers during upstream brownouts; added cache-only fallback.
2025-03-17 Load test run: 50 concurrent refreshes -> upstream queries reduced ~92%, p95 latency improved from ~1.9s to ~420ms.
2025-03-21 Rolled out to 10% prod; monitored upstream backend QPS and TQS p95. No regressions observed.
2025-03-24 Rolled out to 100% prod; added dashboards for cache hit rate + singleflight joins.
2025-03-28 Marked Done after 1 week of stable performance and no new #help reports of telemetry timeouts from bot.
comments: Logan Wright (2025-02-18): Please make sure the cache key includes tenant scope explicitly. We’ve been burned by implicit "all" queries exploding cost. Also +1 to singleflight; we saw identical queries from multiple Slack interactions.
Nadia Rahman (2025-02-26): Route normalization is critical—do not accept raw URL paths. Prefer canonical route_id from the service registry / routing layer labels.
Devon Price (2025-03-04): Bot rendering can handle stale data as long as we get a flag + fetched_at. We’ll show "May be stale" and keep deep links as the escape hatch.
Aisha Bello (2025-03-10): During Sev0s we should prefer returning stale over timing out. Make sure the circuit breaker flips the bot caller into cache-only when upstream is unhealthy.
Jacob Stein (2025-03-17): Load test notes: biggest win was coalescing, not TTL. With TTL=15s and singleflight, a refresh storm stays bounded. Added tqs_singleflight_join_total to quantify.
